cards.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri (Hosea 1:1). Just before this, the call goes out, "Come, let us return to the LORD" (Hosea 6:1). Then God speaks to Ephraim and Judah, two parts of His people that split apart (Isaiah 7:17): "What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah?"

cards.question: God says their loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew. His point is that their loyalty lasts and lasts.

cards.text: Their loyalty is like a morning mist: here at sunrise, GONE before you find your car keys.

cards.question: Therefore God says He has slain them by the words of His mouth. Who does He say He has hewn them by?

cards.text: And His judgments go forth like lightning. Then God says what He desires instead of sacrifice.

cards.question: God says He desires ___, not sacrifice.

cards.text: God desires the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings, too. Friend, that's like handing someone the fanciest cookie box in town and never ONCE asking how they're doing.

cards.question: Like Adam, they have transgressed the ___, and there they were unfaithful to God.

cards.text: Then God gets specific: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.

cards.question: Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests. What do they do on the way to Shechem, a town?

cards.text: Surely they have committed atrocities, and I think this one hurts, because these are priests. And in the house of Israel, God has seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there.

cards.question: With all this going on, God says Israel is defiled.

cards.text: Then God turns to Judah and says a harvest is appointed for them too.

cards.question: God tells Judah a harvest is appointed. When does He say it will be?

answers.text: When He restores His people from captivity
When Judah rebuilds the city walls
When Judah crowns a brand new king

cards.text: God keeps going. Now He talks about what happens when He heals Israel.

cards.question: When God heals Israel, what happens to the iniquity of Ephraim?

cards.text: Like a doctor peeling back the bandage, and the whole room goes OOOH: the crimes of Samaria, a city where Israel's kings reigned (1 Kings 16:29; 2 Kings 17:1), are exposed too. For they practice deceit, thieves break in, and bandits raid in the streets.

cards.question: After all those crimes, God says the people take it to heart that He remembers all their evil.

cards.text: They fail to consider in their hearts that He remembers, but their deeds are all around them, right before His face. That's me wondering where the batch went with crumbs ALL over my apron.

cards.question: The people delight the princes with their lies. And with their evil, they delight the ___.

cards.text: Then God pulls out a picture: they are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker.

cards.question: In God's oven picture, how hot is the baker's oven from the kneading to the rising of the dough?

answers.text: So hot the baker needs not stoke it
Barely warm until the baker stokes it
Cold until the dough is done rising

cards.text: Friend, ovens are MY department, and trust me, one that runs hot ALL by itself is NOT a compliment. On the day of our king, the princes are inflamed with wine.

cards.question: The princes are inflamed with wine, so the king joins hands with those who ___ him.

cards.text: They prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait. All night their anger smolders.

cards.question: Their anger smolders all night, and in the morning it ___ like a flaming fire.

cards.text: Their loyalty was like a morning mist, but their anger shows up in the morning right on time. And God says all of them are hot as an oven.

cards.question: God says all of them are hot as an oven. What do they devour?
In the middle of all this, God says not one of them calls upon Him.
